summary: Phase 3 backend testing complete — 71/71 tests pass (100%) — 25 Phase 1 + 22 Phase 2 + 24 Phase 3. Validated: (1) Profiles CRUD: GET auto-creates default, POST creates secondary with next_number/next_quote=1, PUT updates persist, set-default toggles is_default uniquely, DELETE on only profile -> 400. (2) Profile scoping (CRITICAL): clients/invoices/expenses created in profile A are NOT visible from profile B via X-Profile-Id header — list filters and GET-by-id returns 404 cross-profile. (3) Profile migration: existing users (test_a_*, test_b_*, p2_*, p3_*) auto-get default on /profiles call; data carries profile_id field. (4) Projects: list returns stats {invoiced, expenses, hours, invoices_count}; GET /{id} aggregates linked invoices/expenses/time_entries. (5) Time entries: amount auto = (duration/60)*rate, falls back to project.hourly_rate when missing; convert-to-invoice creates 1 invoice with N items containing 'Xh)' suffix and marks entries billed=true with invoice_id ref. (6) Tags: persisted on clients/invoices/expenses; GET /tags?entity= aggregates {tag, count} sorted desc. (7) Documents: upload (multipart, 4MB cap) returns metadata WITHOUT data_b64; list hides base64; GET /{id} returns raw bytes with correct Content-Type; DELETE works. Invalid entity_type rejected 400. (8) Modelos PDF 303/130/390 all return 200 application/pdf with %PDF magic. (9) ZIP preparar-trimestre: contains all 7 expected entries (libro-ingresos, libro-gastos, iva-repercutido, iva-soportado, modelo-303, modelo-130, resumen JSON) plus facturas/*.pdf when invoices exist; resumen JSON parses with year/quarter/totals. (10) Regression: all Phase 1+2 endpoints still pass after fixing one stale test (PUT /settings was intentionally removed in favour of PUT /profiles/{id}).

minor.issue: Endpoint was removed in Phase 3 (only GET retained for legacy compat returning active profile). If the frontend still calls PUT /settings to persist branding/fiscal data, it will receive 405 — must migrate to PUT /api/profiles/{id}.
No name uniqueness or trim/validation. User can create N profiles named 'Personal' — minor UX issue.
Does not check existence first — silent 200 even if pid doesn't belong to this profile. Consider 404 for clearer client-side handling.
Always uses today as issue_date and empty due_date. Caller cannot specify dates. Also project_id is taken only from entries[0] — mixed-project conversion silently loses info.

entity_id is not validated against an existing record. A document can be uploaded with a non-existent entity_id (it will simply orphan after delete). Consider checking entity_id exists in the relevant collection scoped by profile.
Returns sorted by created_at asc, with no `is_default` first guarantee — frontends that grab profs[0] may not pick the default. Sort by is_default desc, then created_at.

Does not enforce that the previous default is actually unset before setting new — uses 2 separate update_many/one. Functionally fine but not atomic; in concurrent set-default calls, two profiles could briefly be default.

action_items: Frontend audit: replace any PUT /api/settings call with PUT /api/profiles/{active_profile_id}. PUT /settings now returns 405.
Optional: add 404 on DELETE /projects/{pid} when not found; validate entity_id exists in POST /documents.
Optional: in convert-to-invoice, accept issue_date/due_date in payload; reject mixed-project entries (or split into separate invoices).
Optional: ensure GET /profiles returns default profile first (sort is_default desc).
Optional: make set-default atomic via single bulk update or transaction.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1685 lines — even more pressing need to split into routers (auth, profiles, clients, invoices, quotes, payments, projects, time_entries, documents, hacienda, accounting, ai). Maintenance risk is high.

Migration on startup loops over ALL users and runs 6 update_many per user (clients, invoices, expenses, quotes, payments, ai_messages). On a large user base this becomes a startup-time problem; consider gating by a `migrated_to_profiles` flag on each user.

ensure_default_profile is called from get_user_context AND from /auth/login AND from /profiles AND from startup — fine for idempotency but leads to repeated DB writes. Could be optimized with a one-shot cache.

DELETE /profiles/{pid} promotes another profile to default but does NOT delete the data scoped to that profile (clients/invoices/expenses/etc.). Result: orphaned records that won't show up under any profile (invisible). Either cascade delete or refuse with 400 when scope is non-empty.

Documents collection stores base64 in MongoDB — for 4MB files this means up to 5.4MB BSON per doc. With base64 inflation (33%), 4MB raw becomes ~5.5MB stored; close to the 16MB BSON limit if reused for larger files later. Consider GridFS or external object storage long-term.

/tags endpoint allows entity in {client, invoice, expense} but tags also exist on quotes and projects per the codebase — endpoint silently rejects them via Literal. Either expand the Literal or document.
convert-to-invoice does not respect ctx['profile'].default_iva / invoice_series — uses request payload defaults (series='A', iva=21). Honour profile defaults when omitted.
Time entry amount is rounded only to 2 decimals; for sub-minute precision (durations like 5 min @ 47€/h = 3.9166...) rounding may accumulate vs. invoice subtotal recomputation in calculate_totals.

Cleanup test deletes invoices, project, clients, secondary profile.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v --tb=short. All 71 tests pass. PUT /api/settings was removed in Phase 3 — the legacy GET /api/settings returns the active profile data. Frontend must use PUT /api/profiles/{id}. Default profile is auto-created on /auth/login, /auth/register, /profiles, and startup migration. CRITICAL test: when using X-Profile-Id header for cross-profile isolation, send it on EVERY scoped request — list endpoints filter, GET-by-id returns 404 cross-profile, POST writes to header's profile_id. ZIP preparar-trimestre: even with no invoices in period, returns ZIP with the 7 expected entries (CSVs are empty strings for empty books). Modelos PDF endpoints take ~1-3s. The same fixture-scoped clients/invoices/projects from Phase 3 run should be cleaned up by test_zz_cleanup at the end.
rca of the issue: test_settings_get_put failure in test_fakturaflow.py was due to Phase 3 intentionally removing PUT /api/settings (settings are now per-profile, edited via PUT /api/profiles/{id}). Reproduction: requests.put('/api/settings', json=...) returns 405. Mitigation: updated the test to (a) GET /profiles, find default, (b) PUT /profiles/{default.id} with a payload containing the new fiscal_name, (c) re-GET /settings (which returns ctx['profile']) and assert fiscal_name persisted. No backend change required.
